title: Historical ZQX native execution probe is a bounded unmerged diagnostic, not accepted runtime evidence
research_question: What does the historical native PL1–PL3 diagnostic report, and which authority and inference limits must remain attached to its results?
before_state: A successful diagnostic run could be mistaken for a merged production capability or evidence of real-world predictive accuracy.
result: Draft PR #289 reports a bounded diagnostic: 12/12 palace major-star sets matched the supplied structural chart; two engines had zero computed differences across 80 annual snapshots after input gender-label normalization only; 59 W01 wealth rules were evaluated with 15 active and 44 inactive; PL3-N confidence was LOW_CONFIDENCE; the production temporal reaction registry and manifestation/probability registries were empty. The PR remains draft/unmerged, and its tracking Issue #288 is closed as deferred/superseded by #291.
key_insights: The reported comparison is limited to the tested major-star sets and annual snapshot fields, not every chart annotation or all possible dates.
15 active rules are triggered evidence/conditions, not 15 real-world events or probabilities.
The probe records a compatibility alias for PL1 仆役 versus PL2 交友 in its isolated diagnostic; it does not modify canonical code or rules.
The PR body reports 392 historical tests passed, but this task did not rerun the workflow or independently reproduce the result.
negative_findings: Production temporal reaction output was zero because the production reaction registry was empty.
Manifestation ontology/mappings and probability tables were empty in the diagnostic baseline.
No real-world predictive validity, calibration or causal effect is established.
unexpected_findings: The diagnostic surfaced a PL1/PL2 palace-name handoff mismatch (仆役 versus 交友) that was handled only by an explicit alias in the isolated branch.
